title.zh: 卷一百三十二 世襲列傳一: 李茂貞 高萬興 韓遜 李仁福
title.en: Volume 132: Biographies of Descendents 1 - Li Maozhen, Gao Wanxing, Han Xun, Li Renfu
title.raw: 卷一百三十二 世襲列傳一: 李茂貞 高萬興 韓遜 李仁福 Volume 132: Biographies of Descendents 1 - Li Maozhen, Gao Wanxing, Han Xun, Li Renfu

sentences.zh: 李茂貞，本姓宋，名文通，深州博野人。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen, original surname Song, personal name Wentong, a native of Boye in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen was born Song Wentong, a native of Boye in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖鐸，父端。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Duo; his father was Duan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Duo and his father Duan.

sentences.zh: 唐乾符中，鎮州有博野軍，宿衛京師，屯於奉天，文通時隸本軍為市巡，累遷至隊長。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era of Tang, Zhen Prefecture had the Boye Army, which garrisoned the capital as palace guards and was stationed at Fengtian; at that time Wentong served in this army as a market patrol officer and was promoted step by step to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu reign of Tang, the Boye Army from Zhenzhou served as capital guards and was posted at Fengtian; Wentong then belonged to that unit as a market patrolman and rose in stages to company commander.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯闕，博野軍留於鳳翔，時鄭畋理兵於岐下，畋遣文通以本軍敗尚讓之眾於龍尾坡，以功為神策軍指揮使。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital, the Boye Army remained at Fengxiang; at that time Zheng Tian was organizing troops below Qi, and Tian sent Wentong with his native army to defeat Shang Rang's forces at Longwei Slope; for this merit he was made commander of the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao stormed the capital, the Boye Army stayed at Fengxiang; Zheng Tian was then marshaling forces in the Qi region and sent Wentong with his own troops to rout Shang Rang at Longwei Slope, for which he was appointed commander of the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 朱玫之亂，唐僖宗再幸興元，文通扈蹕山南，論功第一，遷檢校太保、同平章事、洋蓬壁等州節度使，賜姓，名茂貞，僖宗親為制字曰正臣。

translations.literal: During Zhu Mei's rebellion, Emperor Xizong of Tang again went to Xingyuan; Wentong escorted the imperial procession south of the mountains and ranked first in merit; he was promoted to acting Grand Guardian, Tongping Zhangshi, and military commissioner of Yang, Peng, Bi and other prefectures; he was granted the surname Li and the name Maozhen; Emperor Xizong personally composed characters for him reading "loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhu Mei's revolt, when Emperor Xizong again fled to Xingyuan, Wentong escorted the court into the southern mountains and was judged foremost in merit; he was promoted to acting Grand Guardian and Tongping Zhangshi, made military commissioner of Yang, Peng, Bi and other prefectures, granted the surname Li and the name Maozhen, and given characters composed by Xizong himself reading "Loyal Minister."

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，王行瑜殺朱玫於京師，李昌符擁兵於岐下，詔茂貞與陳佩等討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei in the capital; Li Changfu held troops below Qi; an edict ordered Maozhen together with Chen Pei and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi, Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei at the capital while Li Changfu massed troops in the Qi region; the court ordered Maozhen, Chen Pei, and others to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 三年，誅昌符，車駕還京，以茂貞為鳳翔節度使，加檢校太尉、兼待中、隴西郡王。

translations.literal: In the third year, Changfu was executed; the imperial carriage returned to the capital; Maozhen was made military commissioner of Fengxiang, with additional appointment as acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Changfu was put to death and the emperor returned to the capital; Maozhen was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang and further honored as acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 大順二年，觀軍容使楊復恭得罪，奔山南，與楊守亮據興元叛，茂貞與王行瑜討平之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dashun, the Army Supervisory Commissioner Yang Fugong fell from favor, fled south of the mountains, and together with Yang Shouliang seized Xingyuan in rebellion; Maozhen and Wang Xingyu suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dashun, Army Supervisory Commissioner Yang Fugong fell from grace and fled into the southern mountains, where he joined Yang Shouliang in holding Xingyuan in revolt; Maozhen and Wang Xingyu put the rebellion down.

sentences.zh: 詔以宰相徐彥若鎮興元，茂貞違詔，表其假子繼徽為留後，堅請旄鉞，昭宗不得已而授之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed the chief minister Xu Yanruo to govern Xingyuan; Maozhen defied the edict and memorialized that his adopted son Jihui should be acting commissioner, firmly requesting the commissioner's baton and axe; Emperor Zhaozong had no choice but to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered chief minister Xu Yanruo to take Xingyuan, but Maozhen defied the order and petitioned that his adopted son Jihui be left in charge, pressing hard for the commissioner's insignia until Zhaozong reluctantly granted them.

sentences.zh: 自是茂貞恃勛恣橫，擅兵窺伺，頗幹朝政，始萌問鼎之志矣。

translations.literal: From this time Maozhen relied on his merit and acted with arrogant license, wielding troops to watch for opportunity and meddling considerably in court politics; he first conceived the ambition to seize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Maozhen traded on his past service to act with impunity, kept his armies poised for advantage, and meddled heavily in court affairs, first nursing the ambition to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 既而逐涇原節度使張球、洋州節度使楊守忠、鳳州刺史滿存，皆奪據其地，奏請子弟為牧伯，朝廷不能制。

translations.literal: Thereafter he drove out Jingyuan military commissioner Zhang Qiu, Yang Prefecture military commissioner Yang Shouzhong, and Feng Prefecture prefect Man Cun, seized all their territories, and memorialized requesting his sons and younger brothers as regional governors; the court could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: He then expelled Zhang Qiu from Jingyuan, Yang Shouzhong from Yangzhou, and Man Cun from Fengzhou, seized their territories, and petitioned to install his sons and brothers as governors, which the court was powerless to prevent.

sentences.zh: 大臣奏議言其過者，茂貞即上章論列，辭旨不遜，奸邪者因之附麗，遂成朋黨，朝政於是隳焉。

translations.literal: When great ministers submitted memorials discussing his faults, Maozhen at once submitted counter-memorials arguing point by point in insubordinate language; wicked men thereupon attached themselves to him, and so a faction was formed; court governance was thereby ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ministers memorialized about his misconduct, Maozhen answered with rebuttals in defiant language; unscrupulous men rallied to him, a faction took shape, and court government collapsed.

sentences.zh: 昭宗性英俊，不任其逼，欲加討伐。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was by nature spirited and resolute and would not endure his coercion; he wished to launch a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong was spirited by nature and would not submit to such pressure; he resolved to attack him.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，命宰臣杜讓能調發軍旅，師未越境，為茂貞所敗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning, he ordered the chief minister Du Rangneng to mobilize armies; the troops had not yet crossed the border when they were defeated by Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianning he ordered chief minister Du Rangneng to raise an army, but the force was beaten by Maozhen before it had even crossed the frontier.

sentences.zh: 茂貞乘勝進屯三橋，京師大震，士庶奔散，天子乃誅中尉西門君遂、李周潼等謝之。

translations.literal: Maozhen pressed his victory and advanced to encamp at Sanqiao; the capital was greatly shaken and officials and commoners fled in disorder; the Son of Heaven then executed the palace eunuchs Ximen Junsui, Li Zhoutong, and others to appease him.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen followed up his victory and encamped at Sanqiao; panic swept the capital and the populace scattered; the emperor then executed palace eunuchs Ximen Junsui, Li Zhoutong, and others to placate him.

sentences.zh: 茂貞嚴兵不解，勢將指闕，抗言讓能之罪，誅之方罷。

translations.literal: Maozhen kept his troops under strict discipline and did not disband them; his momentum was about to point at the palace gates; he openly denounced Rangneng's crimes, and only when Rangneng was executed did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen held his army in readiness and showed no sign of standing down; his forces seemed poised to march on the palace; he loudly demanded Rangneng's punishment, and withdrew only after Rangneng was executed.

sentences.zh: 及韋昭度、李谿為相，茂貞聽崔昭緯之邪說，復沮其事，表昭度等無相業，不可置之臺司，恐亂天下。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi became chief ministers, Maozhen listened to Cui Zhaowei's wicked counsel and again obstructed the matter, memorializing that Zhaodu and the others lacked the capacity for chancellorship and could not be placed in the Secretariat, lest they throw the realm into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi were made chief ministers, Maozhen heeded Cui Zhaowei's malicious advice and blocked the appointments, claiming Zhaodu and the others lacked the talent to serve in the Secretariat and would throw the realm into chaos.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「軍旅之事，吾則與藩臣圖之，朝廷命相，出自朕懷。」

translations.literal: The edict in reply said: "Matters of armies and campaigns I shall deliberate with the frontier lords; appointing ministers at court proceeds from my own intent."
translations.idiomatic: The court replied by edict: "Military affairs I shall discuss with the frontier lords; ministerial appointments at court come from my own judgment."

sentences.zh: 又請授王珙河中節度使，詔報曰：「太原表先至，已許王珂，不可追改。」

translations.literal: He also requested appointing Wang Gong military commissioner of Hezhong; the edict in reply said: "Taiyuan's memorial arrived first; Wang Ke has already been granted the post; it cannot be altered retroactively."
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded that Wang Gong be made military commissioner of Hezhong; the reply edict said: "Taiyuan's memorial arrived first; Wang Ke has already been granted the post, and the decision cannot be reversed."

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年五月，茂貞與王行瑜、韓建稱兵入覲，京師震恐，天子禦樓待之，抗表請殺宰相韋昭度、李谿以謝天下，移王珙於河中。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Qianning, Maozhen together with Wang Xingyu and Han Jian led troops to the capital for an audience; the capital was shaken with fear; the Son of Heaven mounted the tower to receive them; they submitted defiant memorials requesting the execution of chief ministers Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi to appease the realm, and the transfer of Wang Gong to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Qianning, Maozhen, Wang Xingyu, and Han Jian marched on the capital for an audience; terror gripped the city as the emperor mounted the tower to receive them; they submitted defiant memorials demanding the execution of chief ministers Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi to appease the realm and the transfer of Wang Gong to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 既還，留其假子繼鵬宿衛，即閻珪也。

translations.literal: After they returned, he left his adopted son Jipeng to garrison the palace guard — this was Yan Gui.
translations.idiomatic: On their return he left his adopted son Jipeng — Yan Gui — behind as a palace guard garrison.

sentences.zh: 時後唐武皇上表，請討三鎮以寧關輔。

translations.literal: At that time the Martial Emperor of Later Tang submitted a memorial requesting to attack the three garrisons to pacify the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Jin submitted a memorial asking to campaign against the three garrisons to restore order around the capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲七月，太原之師至河中，繼鵬與中尉景宣之子繼晟迫車駕幸鳳翔，昭宗曰：「太原軍未至，鑾輿不可輒動，朕與諸王固守大內，卿等安輯京師，如太原實至，吾可以方略制之。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year, Taiyuan's army reached Hezhong; Jipeng together with the palace eunuch Jing Xuan's son Jisheng forced the imperial carriage to go to Fengxiang; Emperor Zhaozong said: "Taiyuan's army has not yet arrived; the imperial carriage must not be moved lightly; I together with the princes will hold fast within the inner palace; you are to pacify the capital; if Taiyuan truly arrives, I can control them by strategy."
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month the Jin army reached Hezhong; Jipeng and the eunuch Jing Xuan's son Jisheng tried to force the court to flee to Fengxiang; Zhaozong said: "The Jin army has not yet arrived; the imperial carriage must not be moved lightly. I and the princes will hold the inner palace while you restore order in the capital; if Jin forces truly come, I have a plan to deal with them."

sentences.zh: 繼鵬與景宣、中尉駱全權因燔燒東市，中夜大噪。

translations.literal: Jipeng together with Jing Xuan and the palace eunuch Luo Quanquan thereupon set fire to the eastern market; at midnight there was a great uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Jipeng, Jing Xuan, and the eunuch Luo Quanquan then set fire to the eastern market and raised a great clamor at midnight.

sentences.zh: 昭宗登承天門樓避亂，令捧日都將李雲守樓下，繼鵬率眾攻雲。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong ascended the Chengtian Gate tower to escape the turmoil and ordered the Sun-Upholding Division commander Li Yun to guard below the tower; Jipeng led his troops to attack Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong climbed the Chengtian Gate tower to escape the turmoil and ordered Sun-Upholding Division commander Li Yun to hold the foot of the tower; Jipeng led his men against Yun.

sentences.zh: 昭宗憑軒慰諭，繼鵬彎弧大呼，矢拂禦衣，中樓桷。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong leaned on the railing to console and instruct them; Jipeng bent his bow and shouted loudly; an arrow brushed the imperial robe and struck a roof beam.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong leaned on the railing to reason with them; Jipeng drew his bow and shouted; an arrow grazed the imperial robe and struck a roof beam.

sentences.zh: 侍臣掖昭宗下樓還宮，繼鵬即縱火攻宮門。

translations.literal: Attending ministers supported Zhaozong down the tower and back to the palace; Jipeng at once set fire and attacked the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants helped Zhaozong down from the tower and back into the palace; Jipeng immediately set fire to the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 昭宗詔諸王謀其所向，李雲奏曰：「事急矣，請且幸臣營。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong summoned the princes to deliberate where they should go; Li Yun submitted: "The situation is urgent; please for the moment come to my camp."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong summoned the princes to decide their next move; Li Yun said: "Matters are desperate — please come to my camp for the moment."

sentences.zh: 雲乃與扈蹕都將李君慶衛昭宗出啟夏門，駐華嚴寺。

translations.literal: Yun then together with the imperial escort division commander Li Junqing guarded Zhaozong out through the Qixia Gate and halted at Huayan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and imperial escort commander Li Junqing then escorted Zhaozong out through the Qixia Gate to Huayan Temple.

sentences.zh: 晡晚，出幸南山之莎城，駐於石門山之佛寺。

translations.literal: In the late afternoon, he went out to the Sha fortress in the southern mountains and halted at a Buddhist temple on Shimen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening he fled to the Sha fortress in the southern mountains and lodged at a Buddhist temple on Shimen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 是月，武皇至渭北，遣副使王瑰奉表行在，昭宗以武皇為行營都統，進討邠、岐。

translations.literal: That month the Martial Emperor reached the north of the Wei River and sent deputy envoy Wang Gui to present a memorial at the traveling court; Emperor Zhaozong appointed the Martial Emperor overall commander of the field camp to advance and attack Bin and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Prince of Jin reached the north bank of the Wei and sent deputy envoy Wang Gui with a memorial to the traveling court; Zhaozong made him overall commander of the campaign army to advance against Bin and Qi.

sentences.zh: 茂貞懼，斬繼鵬、繼晟，上表待罪，昭宗原之，武皇曰：「不誅茂貞，關輔無由寧謐。」

translations.literal: Maozhen was afraid; he executed Jipeng and Jisheng and submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; Emperor Zhaozong pardoned him; the Martial Emperor said: "If Maozhen is not executed, the capital region cannot be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen grew afraid, executed Jipeng and Jisheng, and submitted a confession; Zhaozong pardoned him, but the Prince of Jin said: "Unless Maozhen is executed, the capital region will never be secure."

sentences.zh: 時附茂貞者奏云：「若太原盡殄邠、岐，必入關輔，京師憂未艾也。」

translations.literal: At that time those attached to Maozhen memorialized saying: "If Taiyuan completely destroys Bin and Qi, they will certainly enter the capital region; the capital's troubles will not yet be ended."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen's supporters then memorialized: "If Jin annihilates Bin and Qi, it will surely march on the capital region, and the capital's troubles will not be over."

sentences.zh: 乃詔武皇與茂貞和。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued for the Martial Emperor and Maozhen to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered the Prince of Jin and Maozhen to make peace.

sentences.zh: 及行瑜誅，武皇班師，茂貞怨望驕橫如故。

translations.literal: When Xingyu was executed, the Martial Emperor withdrew his army; Maozhen's resentment and arrogant license remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyu was executed the Prince of Jin withdrew his army, but Maozhen's resentment and arrogance were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，制授茂貞東川節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year, by imperial ordinance Maozhen was appointed military commissioner of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following fifth month an imperial ordinance appointed Maozhen military commissioner of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 仍命通王、覃王治禁軍於闕下，如茂貞違詔，即討之。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Prince of Tong and the Prince of Tan to train the palace guard army below the palace gates; if Maozhen defied the edict, they were at once to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Tong and Tan were also ordered to drill the palace guards below the palace; if Maozhen defied the edict, they were to attack him at once.

sentences.zh: 茂貞懼，將赴鎮。

translations.literal: Maozhen was afraid and was about to proceed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen grew afraid and prepared to take up his new post.

sentences.zh: 王師至興平，夜自驚潰，茂貞因出乘之，官軍大敗。

translations.literal: The imperial army reached Xingping; at night it panicked and routed itself; Maozhen thereupon sallied forth to take advantage of it, and the government army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army reached Xingping, but panicked and routed itself in the night; Maozhen sallied out to exploit the disorder and routed the government forces completely.

sentences.zh: 車駕倉卒出幸華州，茂貞之眾因犯京師，焚燒宮闕，大掠坊市而去，自此長安大內盡為丘墟矣。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage in haste went out to Hua Prefecture; Maozhen's troops thereupon invaded the capital, burned the palaces, plundered the wards and markets on a great scale and departed; from this time the great inner precinct of Chang'an was entirely reduced to ruins.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled in haste to Huazhou while Maozhen's troops stormed the capital, burned the palaces, and looted the wards before withdrawing; from then on the great inner precinct of Chang'an lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 四年，昭宗復命宰臣孫偓統軍進討，韓建諫止，令茂貞上章請雪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Zhaozong again ordered the chief minister Sun Wo to command armies in an advance punitive campaign; Han Jian remonstrated to stop it and had Maozhen submit a memorial requesting exoneration.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhaozong again ordered chief minister Sun Wo to lead a punitive campaign; Han Jian dissuaded him and had Maozhen petition for exoneration.

sentences.zh: 光化中，加茂貞尚書令、岐王，令其子繼筠以兵宿衛。

translations.literal: During Guanghua, Maozhen was further appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs and Prince of Qi, and his son Jijun was ordered to garrison the palace with troops.
translations.idiomatic: During Guanghua, Maozhen was further made Director of the Department of State Affairs and Prince of Qi, and his son Jijun was stationed at court with troops.

sentences.zh: 天復元年十月，梁祖攻同、華，勢逼京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianfu, the Founder of Liang attacked Tong and Hua; his momentum pressed upon the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianfu, the Liang founder attacked Tong and Hua, threatening the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月六日，繼筠與中尉韓全誨劫昭宗幸鳳翔，茂貞遂與全誨矯詔征兵天下，將討梁祖。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the eleventh month, Jijun together with the palace eunuch Han Quanhui seized Zhaozong and took him to Fengxiang; Maozhen then together with Quanhui forged an edict to levy troops throughout the realm, intending to attack the Founder of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the eleventh month, Jijun and the eunuch Han Quanhui abducted Zhaozong to Fengxiang; Maozhen and Quanhui then forged an edict to levy troops empire-wide for a campaign against the Liang founder.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔允召梁祖引四鎮之兵屯岐下，重溝復壘圍守。

translations.literal: The chief minister Cui Yun summoned the Founder of Liang to lead troops of the four garrisons to encamp below Qi, digging trenches again and again and building ramparts to besiege and hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Cui Yun summoned the Liang founder to bring troops from four garrisons to encamp below Qi, digging trench after trench and building ramparts in a tightening siege.

sentences.zh: 三年，茂貞山南諸州盡為王建所陷，涇、原、秦、隴、邠、鄜、延、夏皆降於汴。

translations.literal: In the third year, all of Maozhen's prefectures south of the mountains were seized by Wang Jian; Jing, Yuan, Qin, Long, Bin, Fu, Yan, and Xia all surrendered to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wang Jian seized all of Maozhen's prefectures south of the mountains, while Jing, Yuan, Qin, Long, Bin, Fu, Yan, and Xia all surrendered to Bian.

sentences.zh: 茂貞獨據孤城，內外援絕，乃請車駕還京，求和於汴，即斬韓全誨等二十人首級送於梁祖。

translations.literal: Maozhen alone held an isolated city; internal and external aid were cut off; he then requested the imperial carriage return to the capital and sought peace with Bian; he at once executed Han Quanhui and twenty others and sent their heads to the Founder of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen held only a lone city with all aid cut off; he then asked the emperor to return to the capital, sued for peace with Bian, and immediately executed Han Quanhui and twenty others, sending their heads to the Liang founder.

sentences.zh: 自是兵力殫盡，垂翅不振，懼梁祖復討，請落尚書令，許之。

translations.literal: From this time his military strength was exhausted and his wings drooped without recovery; fearing the Founder of Liang would again attack, he requested removal from the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his forces were spent and he could no longer recover; fearing another Liang attack, he asked to be stripped of the Directorate of State Affairs, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 〈（《九國誌·李彥琦傳》：彥琦本姓楊氏，鳳翔李茂貞委以心腹之任，易姓李氏，齒於諸子。

translations.literal: (From the "Biography of Li Yanqi" in the 《Jiuguo Zhi》: Yanqi's original surname was Yang; Li Maozhen of Fengxiang entrusted him with duties of intimate confidence, changed his surname to Li, and ranked him with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Li Yanqi in the 《Jiuguo Zhi》: Yanqi was originally surnamed Yang; Li Maozhen of Fengxiang gave him duties of intimate trust, changed his surname to Li, and ranked him with his sons.

sentences.zh: 後昭宗西幸，梁祖迎駕，攻逼岐下者累年，及昭宗東還，長圍方解。

translations.literal: Later when Emperor Zhaozong went west, the Founder of Liang came to receive the imperial carriage and pressed the attack below Qi for many years; only when Zhaozong returned east was the long siege finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhaozong fled west, the Liang founder came to receive the court and pressed the siege below Qi for years; only when Zhaozong returned east was the long encirclement lifted.

sentences.zh: 大軍之後，府庫空竭，彥琦請使甘州以通回鶻，往復二載，美玉、名馬相繼而至，所獲萬計，茂貞賴之。）〉

translations.literal: After the great armies, the treasury was empty and exhausted; Yanqi requested to be sent as envoy to Gan Prefecture to open relations with the Uyghurs; going and returning over two years, fine jade and famous horses arrived in succession; what was obtained numbered in the tens of thousands; Maozhen relied on this.)〉
translations.idiomatic: After the armies departed, the treasury was empty; Yanqi asked to be sent to Ganzhou to open contact with the Uyghurs; over two years' travel fine jade and famous horses arrived in succession, yielding gains in the tens of thousands on which Maozhen relied.)〉

sentences.zh: 及梁祖建號，茂貞與王建會兵於太原，誌圖興復，竟無成功。

translations.literal: When the Founder of Liang established his dynastic title, Maozhen together with Wang Jian joined armies at Taiyuan, intending to restore the Tang, but in the end achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder proclaimed his dynasty, Maozhen and Wang Jian joined forces at Taiyuan in hopes of restoring the Tang, but achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 茂貞疆土危蹙，不遂僭竊之志，但開岐王府，署天官，目妻為皇后，鳴鞘掌扇，宣詞令，一如王者之制，然尚行昭宗之正朔焉。

translations.literal: Maozhen's territory was perilously cramped; he did not realize his usurping ambition; he only opened the Prince of Qi's princely mansion, appointed heavenly officials, called his wife empress, sounded the sword scabbard and wielded the imperial fan, and proclaimed edicts — all exactly like a king's institutions — yet he still followed Emperor Zhaozong's reign era.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen's territory had shrunk to a narrow strip; he never carried out his usurpation, but opened a princely Qi mansion, appointed court officials, styled his wife empress, used royal regalia, and issued proclamations like a sovereign — yet still observed Zhaozong's reign calendar.

sentences.zh: 茂貞鼠形，多智數，軍旅之事，一經耳目，無忘之者。

translations.literal: Maozhen had a rat-like appearance and many stratagems; matters of armies and campaigns — once they passed his eyes and ears, there was nothing he forgot.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen had a rat-like face and was full of stratagems; anything military that reached his eyes or ears he never forgot.

sentences.zh: 性至寬，有部將符昭者，人或告其謀變，茂貞親至其家，去其爪牙，熟寢經宿而還。

translations.literal: His nature was extremely lenient; there was a subordinate commander named Fu Zhao whom someone reported as plotting rebellion; Maozhen personally went to his home, removed his weapons, slept soundly there for a whole night, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was extremely lenient by nature; when someone reported that his officer Fu Zhao was plotting rebellion, Maozhen went to Fu's home in person, disarmed him, slept soundly there overnight, and returned.

sentences.zh: 軍士有鬥而訴者，茂貞曰：「吃令公一碗不托，與爾和解。」

translations.literal: When soldiers fought and came to lodge complaints, Maozhen said: "Eat a bowl of the Commandery Duke's butuo noodles, and I will reconcile you."
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers came to him after brawling, Maozhen said: "Eat a bowl of the Duke's butuo noodles, and I'll settle this between you."

sentences.zh: 遂致上下服之。

translations.literal: Thus superiors and subordinates alike submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he won the loyalty of officers and men alike.

sentences.zh: 尤善事母，母終，茂貞哀毀幾滅性，聞者嘉之。

translations.literal: He was especially filial toward his mother; when his mother died, Maozhen's grief and self-mortification nearly destroyed his nature; those who heard of it praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to his mother; when she died his mourning nearly consumed him, to the admiration of all who heard of it.

sentences.zh: 但禦軍整眾，都無紀律，當食則造庖廚，往往席地而坐，內外持管鑰者，亦呼為司空太保，與夫細柳、大樹之威名，蓋相遠矣。

translations.literal: But in controlling armies and organizing troops he had no discipline at all; when it was time to eat he would go to the kitchens and often sit on the ground; those who held keys inside and outside were also called Acting Grand Guardian; compared with the martial renown of Xiliu and Dashu, he was indeed far removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in commanding troops he observed no discipline at all; at mealtimes he would go to the kitchens and often sit on the ground; even those who held the keys were addressed as Acting Grand Guardian — a far cry from the martial renown of Zhou Yafu and Feng Yi.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗平梁，茂貞自為季父，以書賀之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Maozhen styled himself his uncle and sent a letter of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Maozhen styled himself the emperor's uncle and sent a letter of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 及聞莊宗入洛，懼不自安，方上表稱臣，尋遣其子繼嚴來朝，詔茂貞仍舊官，進封秦王，所賜詔敕不名。

translations.literal: When he heard that Zhuangzong had entered Luoyang, fearing he could not be at ease, he then submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject; soon he sent his son Jiyan to court; an edict ordered Maozhen to retain his former offices, advanced him to Prince of Qin, and the edicts granted him did not use his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Zhuangzong had entered Luoyang he grew fearful, submitted a memorial declaring allegiance, and soon sent his son Jiyan to court; Maozhen was confirmed in his former offices, advanced to Prince of Qin, and addressed in edicts without use of his personal name.

sentences.zh: 又以茂貞宿望耆老，特加優禮。

translations.literal: Because Maozhen was a man of long-standing reputation and advanced age, special courteous treatment was added.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Maozhen's long-standing prestige and advanced age, he was accorded special honors.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，遣中使遣醫藥問訊。

translations.literal: When his illness became grave, the court dispatched palace envoys to send physicians and medicines and inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave, the court sent palace envoys with physicians and medicines to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 同光二年夏四月薨，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the second year of Tongguang he died; he was sixty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of summer in the second year of Tongguang, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 謚曰忠敬。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Loyal and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 子從嚴嗣。

translations.literal: His son Congyan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congyan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 從嚴，茂貞之長子也。

translations.literal: Congyan was Maozhen's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan was Maozhen's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 未冠，授諮議參軍，賜緋魚袋，尋還領彭州副使、鳳翔衙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: Before he came of age he was appointed Advisory Staff Officer, granted the crimson fish tally pouch, and soon returned to hold the posts of deputy commissioner of Peng Prefecture and overall commander within the Fengxiang yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he was made advisory staff officer and granted the crimson fish tally pouch; he soon returned to serve as deputy commissioner of Pengzhou and overall commander of the Fengxiang headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 天復中，自秦王府行軍司馬、檢校太傅出為涇州兩使留後。

translations.literal: During Tianfu, from his posts as campaigning marshal of the Prince of Qin's mansion and acting Grand Mentor he went out to serve as acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs in Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he left his posts as campaigning marshal of the Qin princely mansion and acting Grand Mentor to become acting commissioner of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 茂貞尋承制加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、兼待中，四鎮北庭行軍、彰義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Maozhen soon received an imperial ordinance adding the titles of Grand Preceptor with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen soon received an imperial ordinance promoting him to Grand Preceptor of the First Rank, acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi army.

sentences.zh: 及唐莊宗平梁，茂貞令從嚴入覲，制加從嚴兼中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Liang, Maozhen ordered Congyan to come to court for an audience; by ordinance Congyan was additionally made concurrent Zhongshu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Maozhen sent Congyan to court, and an ordinance made him concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄而茂貞薨，遣奏權知鳳翔軍府事，詔起復，授鳳翔節度、管內觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Soon Maozhen died; he sent a memorial requesting provisional authority over Fengxiang military headquarters affairs; an edict ordered him to resume office from mourning; he was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang and commissioner for observation and disposition within the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Maozhen died he memorialized to take provisional charge of Fengxiang headquarters; the court ordered him to resume office from mourning and appointed him military commissioner of Fengxiang with full circuit authority.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，以魏王繼岌伐蜀，詔充供軍轉運應接使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, as Prince of Wei Jiji attacked Shu, an edict appointed him commissioner for supplying armies, transport, and liaison.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year, when Prince of Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu, an edict appointed Congyan commissioner for supply, transport, and liaison.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，蜀平，繼岌命部署王衍一行東下，至岐，監軍使柴重厚不與符印，促令赴闕。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Shu was pacified; Jiji ordered the escort of Wang Yan and his party eastward; when they reached Qi, the army supervisory commissioner Chai Zhonghou would not give them tally seals and urged them to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Shu was pacified; Jiji ordered Wang Yan and his party escorted east; at Qi, army supervisory commissioner Chai Zhonghou withheld their tally seals and urged them on to the capital.

sentences.zh: 從嚴至華下，聞內難歸鎮，明宗詔誅重厚，從嚴以軍民不擾，重厚之力也，不以前事為隙，上表論救，事雖不允，時議嘉之。

translations.literal: Congyan reached the area below Hua; hearing of internal turmoil he returned to his post; Emperor Mingzong ordered Chai Zhonghou executed; Congyan said that because soldiers and civilians were undisturbed, this was Zhonghou's merit; he did not hold the previous affair against him and submitted a memorial arguing for his rescue; though the matter was not granted, public opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan reached Huazhou, heard of turmoil at court, and returned to his post; Emperor Mingzong ordered Chai Zhonghou executed; Congyan credited Zhonghou with keeping the region calm and, without holding the earlier incident against him, memorialized in his defense; though the plea was denied, contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 天成元年五月，制落起復，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng, by ordinance he was removed from mourning resumption and promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng an ordinance ended his mourning resumption and promoted him to acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，敕曰：「李從嚴等世聯宗屬，任重藩宣，慶善有稱，忠勤甚著。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year an imperial command said: "Li Congyan and others are linked by imperial clan kinship for generations, bear heavy responsibility in frontier governorship and proclamation, are praised for celebrating goodness, and are notably loyal and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month an imperial command said: "Li Congyan and others are of long imperial kinship, bear heavy frontier responsibilities, are praised for their virtue, and are notably loyal and diligent.

sentences.zh: 既預維城之列，宜新定體之文，是降寵光，以隆惇敘，俾煥成家之美，貴從猶子之規，宜於『嚴』、『昶』、『照』上改稱『從』。」

translations.literal: Since they already belong to the ranks that shore up the realm, proper new forms of address should be established; therefore favor and glory are bestowed to exalt kinship ties, so that the beauty of family completion may shine forth and the honored rule for younger imperial clansmen may be observed; on the characters Yan, Chang, and Zhao the character Cong should be used instead."
translations.idiomatic: As members of the imperial clan who shore up the realm, new forms of address are fitting; favor is therefore bestowed to exalt kinship and complete the family's honor according to the rule for younger imperial clansmen: the character Cong should replace Yan, Chang, and Zhao in their names."

sentences.zh: 自長興元年，明宗有事於南郊，從嚴入覲，禮畢，移鎮汴州。

translations.literal: From the first year of Changxing, when Emperor Mingzong performed the southern suburban rites, Congyan came to court for an audience; when the rites were completed, he was transferred to govern Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From the first year of Changxing, when Mingzong performed the southern suburban rites, Congyan came to court; when the rites ended he was transferred to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，復入覲，改天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again came to court for an audience and was changed to military commissioner of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again came to court and was made military commissioner of the Tianping army.

sentences.zh: 及唐末帝起兵於岐下，盡取從嚴家財器仗，以助軍須。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor of Tang raised troops below Qi, he took all of Congyan's family wealth and weapons to supply military needs.
translations.idiomatic: When the last Tang emperor raised troops below Qi, he seized all of Congyan's family wealth and weapons for the army.

sentences.zh: 末帝發離岐城，吏民扣馬，乞以從嚴為帥，末帝許之。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor set out to leave Qi city, officials and commoners seized his horse's bridle and begged that Congyan be made commander; the Last Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When the last emperor prepared to leave Qi, officials and commoners seized his horse's bridle and begged that Congyan be made commander; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，即以從嚴復為鳳翔節度使，仍封秦國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, Congyan was at once restored as military commissioner of Fengxiang and still enfeoffed as Duke of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai he was restored as military commissioner of Fengxiang and continued as Duke of Qin.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖登極，繼封秦王、岐王，累食邑至一萬五千戶，食實封一千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Jin ascended the throne, he was successively enfeoffed as Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi; his cumulative fief households reached fifteen thousand, with actual fief households of one thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, Congyan was successively enfeoffed as Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi; his cumulative fief households reached fifteen thousand, with one thousand five hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，加守太保。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was added as acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 開運三年冬，卒於鎮，年四十有九。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Kaiyun he died at his post; he was forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post in the winter of the third year of Kaiyun, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 從嚴少敏悟，善筆劄，性柔和，無節操。

translations.literal: Congyan in youth was keen and perceptive, skilled at letters, gentle in nature, and without moral firmness.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan was clever and perceptive as a youth, skilled with the brush, gentle by nature, and lacking moral firmness.

sentences.zh: 當莊宗新有天下，因入覲，獻寶裝針珥於皇后宮，時以為佞。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong had newly gained the realm, on coming to court he presented jeweled hairpins and earrings to the empress's palace; at the time this was considered flattery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong had just won the realm, on coming to court he presented jeweled hairpins and earrings to the empress; contemporaries took this for flattery.

sentences.zh: 但進退閑雅，慕士大夫之所為，有請謁者，無賢不肖皆盡其敬。

translations.literal: But in advancing and withdrawing he was leisurely and refined, admired what scholar-officials did, and toward those who requested audiences, whether worthy or unworthy, he showed full respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in bearing he was leisurely and refined, admired the conduct of scholar-officials, and showed full respect to all who sought audience, worthy or not.

sentences.zh: 鎮於岐山，前後二紀，每花繁月朗，必陳勝會以賞之，客有困於酒者，雖吐茵墮幘而無厭色。

translations.literal: Governing at Qi Mountain for two decades before and after, whenever flowers were lush and the moon bright he would always set out splendid gatherings to enjoy them; if guests were overcome by wine, even though they vomited on cushions and lost their headcloths, he showed no sign of displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: He governed at Qishan for some twenty years; whenever flowers bloomed and the moon shone bright he held splendid gatherings, and showed no displeasure even when guests vomited on cushions or lost their caps in drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 左右或有過，未嘗笞責。

translations.literal: If those at his side had faults, he never flogged or reproached them.
translations.idiomatic: He never flogged or rebuked attendants who erred.

sentences.zh: 先人汧、隴之間，有田千頃、竹千畝，恐奪民利，不令理之，致岐陽父老再陳借寇之言，良有以也。

translations.literal: His forebears between Qian and Long had a thousand qing of fields and a thousand mu of bamboo; fearing to seize the people's profit, he would not allow them to be managed, causing the elders of Qiyang again to voice the saying of wishing to borrow an enemy — and they had good reason.
translations.idiomatic: His family held a thousand qing of fields and a thousand mu of bamboo between Qian and Long; fearing to harm the people he would not manage them, so the elders of Qiyang again spoke of wishing he would stay — and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 子永吉，歷數鎮行軍司馬。

translations.literal: His son Yongji served as campaigning marshal in several garrisons in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongji served successively as campaigning marshal in several commands.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：李嚴，岐王之子，昆仲間第六，官至中書令，世謂之「六令公」。

translations.literal: (From the 《Wudai Shi Bu》: Li Yan, son of the Prince of Qi, sixth among his brothers, rose to Zhongshu Ling; the world called him "the Sixth Commandery Duke."
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Li Yan, son of the Prince of Qi, was sixth among his brothers, rose to Director of the Secretariat, and was known as "the Sixth Commandery Duke."

sentences.zh: 性情好戲。

translations.literal: His nature delighted in jesting.
translations.idiomatic: He loved jesting by nature.

sentences.zh: 為鳳翔節度，因生辰，鄰道持賀禮，使畢至，有魏博使少年如美婦人，秦鳳使矬陋且多髯，二人坐又相接，而魏使在下，嚴因曰：「二使車一妍一醜，何不相嘲以為樂事。」

translations.literal: As military commissioner of Fengxiang, on his birthday neighboring circuits brought congratulatory gifts and envoys all arrived; there was a Weibo envoy, a youth like a beautiful woman, and a Qinfeng envoy, short and ugly with a heavy beard; the two were seated next to each other, with the Weibo envoy below; Yan thereupon said: "The two envoys' carriages — one fair, one foul — why not mock each other for amusement?"
translations.idiomatic: As military commissioner of Fengxiang, on his birthday neighboring circuits sent congratulatory gifts and all their envoys arrived; a Weibo envoy was a youth like a beautiful woman, while a Qinfeng envoy was short, ugly, and heavily bearded; seated next to each other with the Weibo envoy below, Yan said: "One envoy fair, one foul — why not banter for our amusement?"

sentences.zh: 魏博使恃少俊，先起曰：「今日不幸與水草大王接席。」

translations.literal: The Weibo envoy, relying on his youth and good looks, rose first and said: "Today I am unfortunate to share a seat with the Water-and-Grass Great King."
translations.idiomatic: The Weibo envoy, confident in his youth and looks, rose first and said: "Today I am unfortunate to share a seat with the Water-and-Grass King."

sentences.zh: 秦鳳使徐起應曰：「水草大王不敢承命，然吾子容貌如此，又坐次相接，得非水草大王夫人耶？」

translations.literal: The Qinfeng envoy slowly rose and replied: "The Water-and-Grass Great King dares not accept that title — yet my lord's appearance is such, and your seats are next to each other; might you not be the Water-and-Grass Great King's wife?"
translations.idiomatic: The Qinfeng envoy rose slowly and replied: "The Water-and-Grass King dares not accept that title — yet with your looks and your seats side by side, might you not be the Water-and-Grass King's wife?"

sentences.zh: 在坐皆笑。）〉

translations.literal: All those seated laughed.) (Editorial supplement ends.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present laughed.)〉

sentences.zh: 從昶生於紈綺，少習華侈，以逸遊宴樂為務，而音律圖畫無不通之。

translations.literal: Congchang was born into brocade and fine silk; in youth he learned luxury and extravagance, made leisurely travel, feasting, and music his occupation, and there was nothing in music, painting, or drawing that he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Congchang was born to luxury, learned extravagance in youth, devoted himself to pleasure and entertainment, and was accomplished in music, painting, and the arts.

sentences.zh: 然性好談笑，喜接賓客，以文翰為賞，曾無虛日。

translations.literal: Yet his nature delighted in jest and conversation; he loved receiving guests and took literary compositions as his pleasure; there was never an idle day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved witty conversation, welcomed guests, delighted in literary exchange, and scarcely let a day pass without such pursuits.

sentences.zh: 復篤信釋氏，時岐下有僧曰阿阇梨，通五天竺語，為士人所歸。

translations.literal: He also devoutly believed in Buddhism; at that time below Qi there was a monk called Acarya who understood the languages of the five regions of India and was followed by scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was also a devout Buddhist; at Qi there was a monk called Acarya who knew the languages of the five Indian regions and was revered by the local gentry.

sentences.zh: 從昶凡歷三鎮，無尤政可褒，無苛法可貶，人用安之，亦將門之令嗣也。

translations.literal: Congchang in all governed three garrisons; there was no outstanding governance to praise, nor harsh laws to condemn; the people were thereby kept at ease — he was also a worthy heir of a military house.
translations.idiomatic: Congchang governed three commands in all; his rule offered little to praise or blame, and the people lived in ease — a creditable heir of a martial clan.

sentences.zh: 弟從照，歷隴州刺史、諸衛大將軍，卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Congzhao served as prefect of Long Prefecture and as a great general of the palace guards, then died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Congzhao served as prefect of Longzhou and as a great general of the palace guards before his death.

sentences.zh: 茂勛，茂貞之從弟也。

translations.literal: Maoxun was Maozhen's younger male cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun was Maozhen's cousin.

sentences.zh: 唐末為鳳翔都將，茂貞表為鄜州節度使，累官至兼侍中。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang he was a capital garrison commander of Fengxiang; Maozhen memorialized him as military commissioner of Fu Prefecture; he rose in office to concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tang he was a Fengxiang garrison commander; Maozhen recommended him as military commissioner of Fuzhou, and he rose to concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁祖之圍鳳翔也，茂勛兵屯岐山，梁祖以羸師誘之，命孔潛率勁兵襲下鄜州，盡俘其家，茂勛遂歸於梁，改名周彜，署元帥府行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When the Founder of Liang besieged Fengxiang, Maoxun's troops were stationed at Qi Mountain; the Founder used a weak army to lure him, ordered Kong Qian to lead crack troops in a surprise descent on Fu Prefecture, and captured his entire family; Maoxun thereupon submitted to Liang, changed his name to Zhou Yi, and was appointed campaigning marshal of the Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder besieged Fengxiang, Maoxun camped at Qishan; the founder baited him with a weak force and sent Kong Qian with elite troops to seize Fuzhou and capture his whole family; Maoxun then submitted to Liang, took the name Zhou Yi, and was made campaigning marshal at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 開平中，為河陽節度使，從梁祖伐鎮州，圍棗強縣。

translations.literal: During Kaiping he was military commissioner of Heyang and followed the Founder of Liang in attacking Zhen Prefecture, besieging Zaoqiang County.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiping he was military commissioner of Heyang and followed the Liang founder against Zhenzhou, besieging Zaoqiang County.

sentences.zh: 時有一民縋城而出，茂勛納之而不疑，一日，其民竊發，以木檐擊茂勛，踣於地，賴左右救至僅免。

translations.literal: At that time a commoner lowered himself from the city wall by rope and came out; Maoxun took him in without suspicion; one day the man launched a surprise attack, struck Maoxun with a wooden eave-pole, knocked him to the ground, and he escaped death only because his attendants rushed to save him.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman once lowered himself from the wall by rope; Maoxun took him in without suspicion, but one day the man attacked by surprise with a wooden beam, knocked him down, and he was saved only by his attendants.

sentences.zh: 居無何，遷金吾上將軍，副王瓚將兵於景店，瓚令分屯西寨，莊宗擊而敗之，降為左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to be a senior general of the Golden Crow Guard, assisting Wang Zan in commanding troops at Jingdian; Zan ordered him to encamp separately at the western stockade; Zhuangzong attacked and defeated him, and he was demoted to senior general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made senior general of the Golden Crow Guard and assisted Wang Zan at Jingdian; when Zan posted him at the western camp, Zhuangzong attacked and defeated him, and he was demoted to senior general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以太子太傅致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he retired as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he retired as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 同光中，復名茂勛。

translations.literal: During Tongguang his original name Maoxun was restored.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongguang his name was restored to Maoxun.

sentences.zh: 天成初，以疾卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he died of illness in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he died of illness at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高萬興，河西人。

translations.literal: Gao Wanxing was a man of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wanxing was a native of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 祖君佐，鄜延節度判官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Junzuo was a judicial aide of the Fu-Yan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Junzuo served as judicial aide to the Fu-Yan military commission.

sentences.zh: 父懷遷，都押衙。

translations.literal: His father Huaiqian was overall escort commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaiqian was overall escort commander.

sentences.zh: 萬興與弟萬金俱有武幹，效用於本軍。

translations.literal: Wanxing and his younger brother Wanjin both had martial ability and rendered service in their native army.
translations.idiomatic: Wanxing and his younger brother Wanjin were both capable soldiers who served in their home army.

sentences.zh: 河西自王行瑜敗後，郡邑皆為李茂貞之所強據，以其將胡敬璋為節度使，萬興為敬璋騎將，昆弟俱有戰功。

translations.literal: After Wang Xingyu's defeat in Hexi, all prefectures and counties were forcibly seized by Li Maozhen, who appointed his general Hu Jingzhang military commissioner; Wanxing was Jingzhang's cavalry commander, and the brothers both had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xingyu's defeat, Li Maozhen seized the Hexi prefectures and appointed his general Hu Jingzhang as commissioner; Wanxing served as Hu's cavalry commander, and both brothers won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 邠州節度使楊崇本者，茂貞之假子也，號李繼徽。

translations.literal: The military commissioner of Bin Prefecture, Yang Chongben, was Maozhen's adopted son and styled himself Li Jihui.
translations.idiomatic: Binzhou military commissioner Yang Chongben was Maozhen's adopted son and took the name Li Jihui.

sentences.zh: 梁祖既弒昭宗，茂貞、繼徽與西川王建之師會於岐陽，以圖興復，皆陳兵關輔，梁祖遣將王重師守雍州、劉知俊守同州以拒之。

translations.literal: After the Founder of Liang murdered Emperor Zhaozong, Maozhen, Jihui, and the army of Wang Jian of Xichuan joined at Qiyang to plan restoration of the Tang; they all deployed troops in the capital region; the Founder sent the generals Wang Chongshi to hold Yong Prefecture and Liu Zhijun to hold Tong Prefecture to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang founder murdered Zhaozong, Maozhen, Jihui, and Wang Jian of Xichuan joined forces at Qiyang to restore the Tang and massed troops around the capital; the founder sent Wang Chongshi to hold Yongzhou and Liu Zhijun to hold Tongzhou against them.

sentences.zh: 天祐五年冬，敬璋卒，崇本以其愛將劉萬子為鄜延帥，萬子以兇暴而失士心。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Tianyou, Jingzhang died; Chongben appointed his favorite general Liu Wanzi commander of Fu-Yan; Wanzi lost the hearts of his troops through cruelty and violence.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year of Tianyou, Jingzhang died; Chongben made his favorite Liu Wanzi commander of Fu-Yan, but Liu lost his men's loyalty through brutality.

sentences.zh: 又，崇本為汴人所攻。

translations.literal: Moreover, Chongben was attacked by men of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Chongben came under attack from Bian forces.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，萬子葬敬璋，將佐皆集於葬所，萬興、萬金因會縱兵攻萬子，殺之，歸款於汴。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, Wanzi buried Jingzhang; officers and aides all gathered at the burial site; Wanxing and Wanjin took advantage of the assembly to unleash troops against Wanzi, killed him, and submitted to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year, when Wanzi buried Jingzhang and all his officers gathered at the funeral, Wanxing and Wanjin seized the moment to attack and kill him, then submitted to Bian.

sentences.zh: 梁祖以萬興為鄜延招撫使，與劉知俊合兵攻收鄜、坊、丹、延等州，梁祖乃分四州為二鎮，以萬興、萬金皆為帥。

translations.literal: The Founder of Liang appointed Wanxing pacification commissioner of Fu-Yan; together with Liu Zhijun he combined armies to attack and recover Fu, Fang, Dan, Yan and other prefectures; the Founder then divided the four prefectures into two commands and made both Wanxing and Wanjin commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang founder made Wanxing pacification commissioner of Fu-Yan; with Liu Zhijun he recovered Fu, Fang, Dan, Yan and other prefectures; the founder then split the four prefectures into two commands under Wanxing and Wanjin.

sentences.zh: 及萬金卒，梁祖以萬興兼彰武、保大兩鎮，累加至太師、中書令，封北平王。

translations.literal: When Wanjin died, the Founder had Wanxing concurrently govern the Zhangwu and Baoda commands; he was promoted step by step to Grand Preceptor and Zhongshu Ling and enfeoffed as Prince of Northern Ping.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanjin's death the founder put Wanxing in charge of both Zhangwu and Baoda, promoted him to Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Northern Ping.

sentences.zh: 莊宗定河洛，萬興來朝，預郊禮陪位，既還鎮，復以舊爵授之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong secured the Yellow River and Luoyang regions, Wanxing came to court, took part in the suburban rites in attendance, and after returning to his post was again granted his former titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong secured the central plains, Wanxing came to court, attended the suburban rites, and on returning to his post was confirmed in his former titles.

sentences.zh: 同光三年十二月，卒於位，以其子允韜權典留後。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Tongguang he died in office; his son Yuntao was given provisional authority as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Tongguang he died in office, and his son Yuntao was left provisionally in charge.

sentences.zh: 允韜，字審機。

translations.literal: Yuntao, style name Shenji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuntao, courtesy name Shenji.

sentences.zh: 初仕梁朝，起家授同州別駕，尋加檢校右僕射，改金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空，充保大軍內外馬步軍指揮使。

translations.literal: He first served the Liang court, beginning his career as vice-prefect of Tong Prefecture; soon he was added as acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Pouch and acting Minister of Works, and appointed commander of the inner and outer horse and foot armies of the Baoda army.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career under Liang as vice-prefect of Tongzhou, was soon made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Minister of Works, and commander of the Baoda army's horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 唐同光中，檢校太保，充保大軍兩使留後。

translations.literal: During Tongguang of Tang he was acting Grand Guardian and acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs of the Baoda army.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang Tongguang he was acting Grand Guardian and acting commissioner of the Baoda army.

sentences.zh: 萬興卒，允韜自理所奔喪。

translations.literal: When Wanxing died, Yuntao rushed from his post to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanxing died, Yuntao left his post to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 天成初，起復檢校太傅，充延州節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he resumed office from mourning as acting Grand Mentor and military commissioner of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he resumed office from mourning as acting Grand Mentor and military commissioner of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，移鎮邢州，頃之，為右龍武統軍，未幾，授滑州節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing he was transferred to govern Xing Prefecture; shortly thereafter he became overall commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard; before long he was appointed military commissioner of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing he was transferred to Xingzhou, soon made overall commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard, and shortly afterward appointed military commissioner of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年八月，卒於任，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Qingtai he died in office; he was forty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the eighth month of the second year of Qingtai, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太師。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 韓遜，本靈州之列校也。

translations.literal: Han Xun was originally a rank-and-file officer of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xun was originally a junior officer of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會唐季之亂，因據有其地，朝廷乃授以節鉞。

translations.literal: When the disorders of the late Tang arose, he seized and held that territory; the court thereupon granted him the commissioner's baton and axe.
translations.idiomatic: During the late Tang disorders he seized the region, and the court granted him the commissioner's insignia.

sentences.zh: 梁初，累加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang he was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Commandant and Tongping Zhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang he was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Commandant and Tongping Zhangshi.

sentences.zh: 開平中，梁將劉知俊自同州叛歸鳳翔，李茂貞以地褊不能容，乃借兵以窺靈武，且圖牧圉之地。

translations.literal: During Kaiping, the Liang general Liu Zhijun rebelled from Tong Prefecture and returned to Fengxiang; Li Maozhen, finding his territory too narrow to accommodate him, then borrowed troops to probe Lingwu and also aimed at pasture lands.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiping, Liang general Liu Zhijun rebelled from Tongzhou and fled to Fengxiang; Maozhen's territory was too cramped to hold him, so he borrowed troops to probe Lingwu and seize pasturelands.

sentences.zh: 知俊乃帥邠、岐、秦、涇之師數萬攻遜於靈州，遜竭力以拒之，久之，知俊遁去。

translations.literal: Zhijun then led tens of thousands of troops from Bin, Qi, Qin, and Jing to attack Xun at Ling Prefecture; Xun resisted with all his strength; after a long time Zhijun fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun then led tens of thousands from Bin, Qi, Qin, and Jing against Xun at Lingzhou; Xun resisted with all his strength until Zhijun eventually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 梁祖嘉之，自是累加官至中書令，封潁川郡王。

translations.literal: The Founder of Liang commended him; from this time he was repeatedly promoted in office to Zhongshu Ling and enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang founder commended him; thereafter he rose to Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 遜亦善於為理，部民請立生祠堂於其地，梁祖許之，仍詔禮部待郎薛廷珪撰文以賜之，其廟至今在焉。

translations.literal: Xun was also skilled in governance; the people of his command requested that a living shrine be erected in his territory; the Founder granted this and further ordered the Vice Minister of Rites Xue Tinggui to compose a text and bestow it; the shrine stands to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was also a capable administrator; his people asked to erect a living shrine in his honor, which the founder approved, and he ordered Vice Minister of Rites Xue Tinggui to compose an inscription; the shrine still stands.

sentences.zh: 貞明初，遜卒於鎮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming, Xun died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenming, Xun died in office.

sentences.zh: 洙，遜之子也。

translations.literal: Zhu was Xun's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was Xun's son.

sentences.zh: 遜卒，三軍推為留後，梁末帝聞之，起復正授靈武節度使、特進、檢校太傅、同平章事。

translations.literal: When Xun died, the three armies pushed Zhu as acting commissioner; when the Last Emperor of Liang heard of it, he ordered mourning resumption and formally appointed him military commissioner of Lingwu, Special Advancement, acting Grand Mentor, and Tongping Zhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun died the army made Zhu acting commissioner; the last Liang emperor ordered him to resume office and formally appointed him military commissioner of Lingwu, Special Advancement, acting Grand Mentor, and Tongping Zhangshi.

sentences.zh: 貞明四年春，靈武將軍尚貽敏等上言，洙已服闋，乞落起復。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Zhenming, the Lingwu generals Shang Yimin and others submitted that Zhu had completed mourning and begged removal from mourning resumption.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Zhenming, Lingwu generals including Shang Yimin memorialized that Zhu had completed mourning and asked to end his mourning resumption.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝令中書商量，宰臣奏曰：「舊例藩鎮落起復，如先人已是一品階，即與加爵；

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang ordered the Secretariat to deliberate; the chief ministers submitted: "By old precedent, when a frontier command ends mourning resumption, if the forebear already held first-rank status, a noble title is granted;
translations.idiomatic: The last Liang emperor ordered the Secretariat to deliberate; the chief ministers submitted: "By precedent, when a frontier commander ends mourning resumption, if his father already held first rank, a noble title is granted;

sentences.zh: 如未是一品階，即合加階。」

translations.literal: if the forebear had not yet reached first rank, a rank promotion is appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: if the father had not yet reached first rank, a promotion in rank is appropriate."

sentences.zh: 乃授洙開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Zhu was then appointed Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was then appointed Grand Preceptor of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗、明宗累加官爵。

translations.literal: Emperors Zhuangzong and Mingzong of Tang repeatedly added to his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Tang emperors Zhuangzong and Mingzong repeatedly added to his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 天成四年夏，洙卒，朝廷以其弟澄為朔方軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Tiancheng, Zhu died; the court appointed his younger brother Cheng acting commissioner for observation of the Shuofang army.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year of Tiancheng Zhu died, and the court appointed his younger brother Cheng acting commissioner of the Shuofang army.

sentences.zh: 是歲，有列校李賓作亂，部內不安，乃遣使上表請帥於朝廷，明宗命前磁州刺史康福為朔方河西等軍節度、靈威雄警涼等州觀察處置度支、溫池榷稅等使，仍遣福領兵萬人赴鎮，其後靈武遂受代焉。

translations.literal: That year the rank-and-file officer Li Bin rebelled and the command was unsettled; they therefore sent envoys with a memorial requesting a commander from court; Emperor Mingzong appointed the former prefect of Ci Prefecture Kang Fu military commissioner of the Shuofang and Hexi armies, commissioner for observation, disposition, and fiscal administration of Ling, Wei, Xiong, Jing, and Liang prefectures, and commissioner of the Wenchi monopoly tax, and further sent Fu leading ten thousand troops to take up the post; thereafter Lingwu was replaced.
translations.idiomatic: That year junior officer Li Bin rebelled and unsettled the region; envoys memorialized for a court-appointed commander; Mingzong appointed former Cizhou prefect Kang Fu military commissioner of Shuofang and Hexi with full circuit authority, and sent him with ten thousand men to take the post; Lingwu was thereafter brought under direct court control.

sentences.zh: 李仁福，世為夏州牙將，本拓拔氏之族也。

translations.literal: Li Renfu, for generations a yamen officer of Xia Prefecture, was originally of the Toba clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renfu came from a line of Xiazhou yamen officers and was originally of the Toba clan.

sentences.zh: 唐乾符中，有拓拔思恭為夏州節度使，廣明之亂，唐僖宗在蜀，詔以思恭為京城西北收復都統，預破黃巢有功，僖宗賜姓，故仁福亦以李為氏。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era of Tang there was Toba Sigong as military commissioner of Xia Prefecture; during the disorders of Guangming, Emperor Xizong of Tang was in Shu; an edict appointed Sigong overall commander for recovery of the northwest of the capital region; he took part in defeating Huang Chao with merit; Xizong granted him the surname Li; therefore Renfu also took Li as his clan name.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang Qianfu, Toba Sigong was military commissioner of Xiazhou; during the Guangming disorders, when Xizong was in Shu, Sigong was made overall commander for recovering the northwest around the capital, helped defeat Huang Chao, and was granted the surname Li; Renfu therefore also bore the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 思恭卒，弟思諫繼之。

translations.literal: When Sigong died, his younger brother Sijian succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sigong died, his younger brother Sijian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 梁開平元年，授思諫檢校太尉、兼待中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiping of Liang, Sijian was appointed acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Liang Kaiping, Sijian was appointed acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二年，思諫卒，三軍立其子彜昌為留後，尋起復，正授旄鉞。

translations.literal: In the second year, Sijian died; the three armies installed his son Yichang as acting commissioner; soon mourning resumption followed, and he was formally granted the baton and axe.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Sijian died; the army made his son Yichang acting commissioner, soon confirmed after mourning resumption with the commissioner's insignia.

sentences.zh: 三年春，牙將高宗益等作亂，彜昌遇害，時仁福為蕃部指揮使，本州軍吏迎立仁福為帥。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, the yamen generals Gao Zongyi and others rebelled and Yichang was killed; at that time Renfu was commander of the tribal forces; the military officials of the prefecture welcomed and installed Renfu as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year yamen generals including Gao Zongyi rebelled and killed Yichang; Renfu was then tribal commander, and the local military officials installed him as commander.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，梁祖降制授仁福檢校司空，充定難軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year the Founder of Liang issued an ordinance appointing Renfu acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Dingnan army.
translations.idiomatic: That fourth month the Liang founder appointed Renfu acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Dingnan army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，後唐武皇遣大將周德威會邠、鳳之師五萬同攻夏州，仁福固守月餘，梁援軍至，德威遁去，梁祖喜之，超授檢校太保、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long the Martial Emperor of Later Tang sent the great general Zhou Dewei to join fifty thousand troops from Bin and Feng in a joint attack on Xia Prefecture; Renfu held firm for more than a month; Liang relief troops arrived and Dewei fled; the Founder was pleased and specially promoted him to acting Grand Guardian and Tongping Zhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Jin sent Zhou Dewei with fifty thousand troops from Bin and Feng to attack Xiazhou; Renfu held out for over a month until Liang reinforcements arrived and Dewei withdrew; the founder was pleased and specially promoted him to acting Grand Guardian and Tongping Zhangshi.

sentences.zh: 仁福自梁貞明、龍德及後唐同光中，累官至檢校太師、兼中書令，封朔方王。

translations.literal: From Liang Zhenming and Longde through Later Tang Tongguang, Renfu rose in office step by step to acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Zhongshu Ling, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang Zhenming and Longde through Later Tang Tongguang, Renfu rose to acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Prince of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 長興四年三月，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Changxing he died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the third month of the fourth year of Changxing.

sentences.zh: 其年追封虢王。

translations.literal: That year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guo.

sentences.zh: 子彜超嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yichao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yichao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 彜超，仁福之次子也。

translations.literal: Yichao was Renfu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Yichao was Renfu's second son.

sentences.zh: 歷本州左都押衙、防遏使，仁福卒，三軍立為帥，矯為仁福奏云：「臣疾已甚，已委彜超權知軍州事，乞降真命。」

translations.literal: He served in succession as left overall escort commander and defense commissioner of the prefecture; when Renfu died the three armies installed him as commander; he forged a memorial in Renfu's name saying: "My illness is already grave; I have already entrusted Yichao with provisional authority over military and prefectural affairs; I beg that a true appointment be granted."
translations.idiomatic: He had served as left overall escort commander and defense commissioner; when Renfu died the army made him commander and forged a memorial in Renfu's name: "My illness is grave; I have entrusted Yichao with provisional authority; I beg a formal appointment."

sentences.zh: 明宗聞之，遂以彜超為延州留後，以延帥安從進為夏州留後。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong heard of this, he then appointed Yichao acting commissioner of Yan Prefecture and the Yan commander An Congjin acting commissioner of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong then appointed Yichao acting commissioner of Yanzhou and Yan commander An Congjin acting commissioner of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮不從命，詔邠州節度使藥彥稠、宮苑使安從益等率師援送從進赴鎮，仍降詔諭之云：

translations.literal: The court feared he would not obey; an edict ordered the military commissioner of Bin Prefecture Yao Yanchou, the palace park commissioner An Congyi, and others to lead troops to escort Congjin to his post, and further issued an edict instructing them, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disobedience, the court ordered Binzhou commissioner Yao Yanchou, palace park commissioner An Congyi, and others to escort Congjin to his post with troops, and issued this instruction:

sentences.zh: 近據西北藩鎮奏，定難軍節度使李仁福薨。

translations.literal: Recently, according to memorials from the northwestern frontier commands, the military commissioner of the Dingnan army, Li Renfu, has died.
translations.idiomatic: Recent memorials from the northwest report that Dingnan military commissioner Li Renfu has died.

sentences.zh: 朕以仁福自分戎閫，遠鎮塞垣，威惠俱行，忠孝兼著。

translations.literal: We consider that Renfu, from his own origins in the military frontier, governed far off on the border ramparts, combining authority and kindness, and displaying both loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Renfu rose from the military frontier to govern the distant borderlands, combining authority with kindness and showing both loyalty and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 當本朝播越之後，及先皇興復之初，爰及眇躬，益全大節，統臨有術，遠邇咸安。

translations.literal: In the time after our dynasty was driven into exile, and at the beginning of the former emperor's restoration, down to Our slight person, he further preserved great integrity; his governance was skilled, and far and near were all at peace.
translations.idiomatic: From the dynasty's exile through the former emperor's restoration down to Our reign, he preserved his integrity, governed skillfully, and kept far and near at peace.

sentences.zh: 委伏方深，雕殞何速，忽窺所奏，深愴予懷。

translations.literal: Our reliance on him had just deepened — how swiftly the eagle fell! Suddenly reading the memorial submitted, We are deeply stricken in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: Our reliance on him had only deepened — how swiftly he fell! Reading the memorial, We are deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 不朽之功，既存於社稷；

translations.literal: His imperishable merit already rests with the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: His imperishable service already rests with the state;

sentences.zh: 有後之慶，宜及於子孫。

translations.literal: the blessing of posterity should extend to his sons and descendants.
translations.idiomatic: the blessing of posterity should extend to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 但以彼藩地處窮邊，每資經略，厥子年才弱冠，未歷艱難，或虧駕御之方，定起奸邪之便。

translations.literal: Yet because that command lies in the remotest border, where constant strategic planning is required, his son has only just reached weak adulthood and has not yet experienced hardship; he may lack the methods of control and surely give wicked men their opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet that command lies on the remotest frontier and requires constant strategy; his son has only just come of age, lacks experience, may prove unable to govern, and could give wicked men their chance.

sentences.zh: 其李彜超已除延州節度觀察留後，便勒赴任。

translations.literal: Li Yichao has already been removed and appointed acting commissioner for observation of Yan Prefecture; he is to be compelled to proceed to his post at once.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yichao has been appointed acting commissioner of Yanzhou and is to proceed to his post at once.

sentences.zh: 但夏、銀、綏、宥等州，最居邊遠，久屬亂離，多染夷狄之風，少識朝遷之命，既乍當於移易，宜普示於渥恩。

translations.literal: But Xia, Yin, Sui, You and other prefectures lie in the most remote borderlands; for long they have belonged to turmoil and separation; many are steeped in barbarian ways and know little of the court's transforming commands; since they have suddenly undergone change, generous favor should be broadly displayed.
translations.idiomatic: But Xia, Yin, Sui, You and other prefectures lie on the farthest frontier, long torn by disorder, steeped in frontier ways and little acquainted with court authority; since they face sudden change, generous favor should be shown broadly.

sentences.zh: 應夏、銀、綏、宥等州管內，罪無輕重，常赦所不原者，並公私債負、殘欠稅物，一切並放；

translations.literal: Within the jurisdictions of Xia, Yin, Sui, You and other prefectures, crimes whether light or heavy, even those not normally pardoned in regular amnesties, together with public and private debts and remaining unpaid taxes — all are to be entirely remitted;
translations.idiomatic: Within Xia, Yin, Sui, You and other prefectures, all crimes, even those not normally pardoned, together with public and private debts and unpaid taxes, are to be remitted entirely;

sentences.zh: 兼自刺史、指揮使、押衙已下，皆勒依舊，各與改轉官資。

translations.literal: and from prefects, commanders, and escort commanders downward, all are to be compelled to remain in their former posts, each granted a change and promotion in official status.
translations.idiomatic: and from prefects, commanders, and escort officers downward, all are to remain in their posts and receive promotions in rank.

sentences.zh: 朕自總萬幾，惟宏一德，內安華夏，外撫戎夷，先既懷之以恩，後必示之以信。

translations.literal: Since We assumed the myriad affairs of state, We have sought only to enlarge unified virtue, pacifying the Hua-Xia within and soothing the barbarians without; first We have embraced them with kindness, afterward We shall certainly show them good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne We have sought unified virtue, pacifying China within and soothing the frontier peoples without — first embracing them with kindness, then showing them good faith.

sentences.zh: 且如李從嚴之守岐、隴，疆土極寬；

translations.literal: Consider, for example, Li Congyan's holding of Qi and Long — his territory was extremely broad;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Li Congyan, who held Qi and Long with vast territory;

sentences.zh: 高允韜之鎮鄜、延，甲兵亦眾。

translations.literal: Gao Yuntao's governing of Fu and Yan — his armored troops were also numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuntao, who governed Fu and Yan with numerous troops.

sentences.zh: 咸能識時知變，舉族歸朝。

translations.literal: Both were able to recognize the times and know how to adapt, and brought their whole clans to submit to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Both recognized the times, adapted, and brought their clans to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 從嚴則見鎮大梁，允韜則尋除鉅鹿，次及昆仲，並建節旄，下至將僚，悉分符竹。

translations.literal: Congyan was then seen governing Daliang; Yuntao was soon appointed to Julu; next their brothers all received commander's banners and axes; down to their generals and aides, all were granted tally tablets of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan was then posted to Daliang, Yuntao soon to Julu; their brothers received commanders' insignia, and even their officers were granted commissions.

sentences.zh: 又若王都之貪上谷，李賓之吝朔方，或則結構契丹，偷延旦夕；

translations.literal: Or again, like Wang Du's greed for Shanggu and Li Bin's stinginess over Shuofang — some colluded with the Khitan to steal a few days more;
translations.idiomatic: Or like Wang Du, who coveted Shanggu, and Li Bin, who clung to Shuofang — some colluded with the Khitan to buy a little more time;

sentences.zh: 或則依憑党項，竊據山河。

translations.literal: others relied on the Tangut and secretly seized mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: others relied on the Tangut and seized territory by force.

sentences.zh: 不稟除移，惟謀旅拒，才興討伐，已見覆亡。

translations.literal: They did not await dismissal and transfer, but only plotted armed resistance; as soon as punitive campaigns were launched, they were already seen overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: They ignored court orders and plotted resistance; as soon as campaigns were launched, they were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 何必廣引古今，方明利害；

translations.literal: Why must one broadly cite antiquity and the present to make clear advantage and harm?
translations.idiomatic: Why cite antiquity at length to show advantage and harm?

sentences.zh: 只陳近事，聊諭將來。

translations.literal: It is enough to set forth recent events merely to instruct what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: Recent events alone suffice to instruct the future.

sentences.zh: 彼或要覆族之殃，則王都、李賓足為鑒戒；
