translations.literal: If they desire the calamity of clan extinction, Wang Du and Li Bin are sufficient as warnings;
translations.idiomatic: If they seek the destruction of their clans, Wang Du and Li Bin are warning enough;

sentences.zh: 彼或要全身之福，則允韜、從嚴可作規繩。

translations.literal: if they desire the blessing of preserving their persons whole, Yuntao and Congyan may serve as measuring cords.
translations.idiomatic: if they seek to preserve themselves, Yuntao and Congyan may serve as models.

sentences.zh: 朕設兩途，爾宜自擇。

translations.literal: We have set out two paths; you should choose for yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: We have set out two paths; choose for yourselves.

sentences.zh: 或慮將校之內、親要之間，幸彼幼沖，恣其熒惑，遂成騷動，致累生靈。

translations.literal: We fear that among the commanders or among close associates, taking advantage of his youth and tender age, they may indulge in delusive persuasion, thereby producing turmoil and bringing suffering upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: We fear that among his officers or intimates, taking advantage of his youth, some may mislead him into turmoil that harms the people.

sentences.zh: 今特差邠州節度使藥彥稠部領馬步兵士五萬人騎，送安從進赴任，從命者秋毫勿犯，違命者全族必誅，先令後行，有犯無赦雲。

translations.literal: Now We specially dispatch the military commissioner of Bin Prefecture Yao Yanchou to lead fifty thousand horse and foot soldiers to escort An Congjin to his post; those who obey will not have even an autumn hair harmed; those who defy will have their whole clans certainly executed; orders precede action, and violations will not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: We now specially dispatch Binzhou commissioner Yao Yanchou with fifty thousand horse and foot to escort An Congjin to his post; those who obey will not be harmed in the slightest; those who defy will have their whole clans executed; orders precede action, and violations will not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 其年夏四月，彜超上言：「奉詔授延州留後，已迎受恩命，緣三軍百姓擁隔，未放赴任。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer that year, Yichao submitted: "Having received the edict appointing me acting commissioner of Yan Prefecture, I have already welcomed and accepted the gracious command; but because the three armies and the common people block and detain me, I have not been allowed to proceed to my post."
translations.idiomatic: That fourth month of summer Yichao memorialized: "I have received the edict appointing me acting commissioner of Yanzhou and accepted the gracious command, but the army and populace block my departure."

sentences.zh: 明宗遣閣門使蘇繼彥賫詔促之。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong dispatched the Gatekeeper Envoy Su Jiyan bearing an edict to urge him on.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent gatekeeper envoy Su Jiyan with an edict to urge him on.

sentences.zh: 五月，安從進領軍至城下，彜超不受代，從進駐軍以攻之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, An Congjin led his army to the foot of the city wall; Yichao would not accept replacement; Congjin encamped his army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month An Congjin brought his army to the city; Yichao refused to yield; Congjin encamped and attacked.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，彜超昆仲登城謂從進曰：「孤弱小鎮，不勞王師攻取，虛煩國家餉運，得之不武，為仆聞天子，乞容改圖。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Yichao and his brothers mounted the wall and said to Congjin: "This is a lone, small command; it does not require the imperial army to take it by force, vainly troubling the state's supply transport — to gain it would be unmartial; allow me to report to the Son of Heaven and beg permission to change our plan."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yichao and his brothers mounted the wall and told Congjin: "This is a small, isolated command; it need not trouble the imperial army or state supplies — to take it by force would be unworthy; let me report to the emperor and beg leave to reconsider."

sentences.zh: 時又四面党項部族萬餘騎，薄其糧運，而野無芻牧，關輔之人，運鬥粟束槁，動計數千，窮民泣血，無所控訴，復為蕃部殺掠，死者甚眾，明宗聞之，乃命班師。

translations.literal: At that time moreover, on all four sides more than ten thousand Tangut tribal horsemen pressed upon their grain transport; yet in the wilds there was no fodder for grazing; the people of the capital region transported grain by the dou and bundles of hay, each movement reckoned in the thousands; the destitute wept blood with nowhere to appeal; they were again killed and plundered by the tribal forces — the dead were very many; when Emperor Mingzong heard of this, he ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile more than ten thousand Tangut horsemen pressed their supply lines from all sides while the countryside offered no fodder; people of the capital region hauled grain and hay in thousands of loads; the poor wept blood with nowhere to appeal and were again killed and plundered by tribal forces; the dead were many; when Mingzong heard of this he ordered withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 彜超亦上表謝罪，乃授彜超檢校司徒，充定難軍節度使，既而修貢如初。

translations.literal: Yichao also submitted a memorial confessing guilt; he was then appointed acting Minister of Education and military commissioner of the Dingnan army; before long he resumed tribute as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yichao also submitted a confession; he was appointed acting Minister of Education and military commissioner of the Dingnan army, and soon resumed tribute as before.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the second year of Qingtai.

sentences.zh: 弟彜興襲其位。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yixing succeeded to his position.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yixing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 彜興，本名彜殷，宋受命之初，以犯廟諱故改之。

translations.literal: Yixing, original personal name Yiyin, at the beginning of Song's receiving the Mandate had his name changed because it violated a taboo of the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing, originally named Yiyin, had his name changed at the founding of Song because it violated an imperial temple taboo.

sentences.zh: 彜超既卒，時彜興為夏州行軍司馬，三軍推為留後，唐末帝聞之，正授定難軍節度使。

translations.literal: After Yichao died, at that time Yixing was campaigning marshal of Xia Prefecture; the three armies pushed him as acting commissioner; when the Last Emperor of Tang heard of it, he formally appointed him military commissioner of the Dingnan army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yichao died, Yixing was campaigning marshal of Xiazhou; the army made him acting commissioner, and the last Tang emperor formally appointed him military commissioner of the Dingnan army.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu of Jin he was added as acting Grand Commandant and Tongping Zhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin Tianfu he was made acting Grand Commandant and Tongping Zhangshi.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was added as acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，彜興弟綏州刺史彜敏與其黨作亂，為彜興所逐，彜敏奔延州，彜興押送到闕，骨肉二百餘口，朝延以彜興之故，縶送本道斬之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, Yixing's younger brother Yimin, prefect of Sui Prefecture, rebelled together with his faction; he was driven out by Yixing; Yimin fled to Yan Prefecture; Yixing escorted him to court — more than two hundred kinsmen; the court, for Yixing's sake, bound them and sent them back to his circuit for execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year, Yixing's brother Yimin, prefect of Suizhou, rebelled with his faction; Yixing drove him out; Yimin fled to Yanzhou; Yixing escorted him to court with more than two hundred kinsmen; for Yixing's sake the court sent them back to his circuit for execution.

sentences.zh: 開運元年春，詔以彜興為契丹西南面招討使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Kaiyun, an edict appointed Yixing pacification commissioner of the Khitan southwestern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Kaiyun an edict appointed Yixing pacification commissioner on the Khitan southwestern frontier.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐元年春，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Qianyou of Han he was added as concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Han Qianyou he was made concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 是歲，李守貞叛於河中，潛使人構之，彜興為之出師，駐於延州之北境，既而聞守貞被圍，乃收軍而退。

translations.literal: That year Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong; he secretly sent men to incite him; Yixing marched out an army on his behalf and encamped on the northern border of Yan Prefecture; soon hearing that Shouzhen was besieged, he then withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and secretly incited Yixing, who marched out and encamped on Yanzhou's northern border; hearing Shouzhen was besieged, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，累加至守太傅、兼中書令，封西平王。

translations.literal: During Xiande of Zhou he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Zhongshu Ling, and enfeoffed as Prince of Western Ping.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhou Xiande he rose to Acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Prince of Western Ping.

sentences.zh: 皇朝建隆元年春，制加守太尉，始改名彜興。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Jianlong of the Imperial Dynasty, by ordinance he was added as Acting Grand Commandant and first given the name Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Song Jianlong an ordinance made him Acting Grand Commandant and first gave him the name Yixing.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年秋，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Qiande he died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the autumn of the fifth year of Qiande.

sentences.zh: 制贈太師，追封夏王。

translations.literal: By ordinance he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: An ordinance posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed him as Prince of Xia.

sentences.zh: 子光睿繼其位，其後事具皇朝日曆。

translations.literal: His son Guangrui succeeded to his position; subsequent events are fully recorded in the calendar of the Imperial Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guangrui succeeded him; subsequent events are recorded in the Song court calendar.
